highlights: OpenAI's chief scientist argues for perplexity as a shared metric for comparing models and setting safety standards, and reports pretraining losses below 0.8 alongside the emergence of transformative capabilities in cybersecurity and mathematics.

items.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes perplexity as a shared AI metric
items.summary: Jakub Pachocki argues for establishing perplexity, or equivalently cross-entropy loss, as a metric that model developers can use to compare progress and shape shared safety standards. He reports that OpenAI has reached losses below 0.8, alongside the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics, and proposes common limits tied to perplexity until AI behavior can be understood and monitored.

evidence.quote: OpenAI November 22, 2026 Research Safety Perplexity and Intelligence By Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI Share From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities.
In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards.
As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI.
2 , 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions.
The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5.
Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics.

Given that the main way new surprising capabilities emerge is by progress on compression, a measure rooted in perplexity could give us a shared benchmark for general intelligence, regardless of the degree of automation of the development process.

I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models and red-team safety cases for them by the time they are first used, including shared transparency standards.

I further propose common limits , based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors).

items.title: Superpowers packages a software development methodology for coding agents
items.summary: Superpowers is described as an agentic skills framework and software development methodology that works, built on composable skills and initial instructions. The agent works from a spec through an implementation plan and a subagent-driven development process, and the skills are said to trigger automatically; it is available through the official Claude plugin marketplace and the official Codex plugin marketplace.

evidence.quote: Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.
It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent.
Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow.
Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward.
It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.
And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special.
Superpowers is available via the official Claude plugin marketplace
Superpowers is available via the official Codex plugin marketplace .
gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

items.title: Firecrawl offers local and hosted knowledge infrastructure for agents
items.summary: Firecrawl provides knowledge infrastructure for agents, with a local binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into an AI agent as an MCP server, and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost. The hosted service adds search and the 550+ data providers in Firecrawl Alexandria, while local routes need no API key and JavaScript-rendered pages, PDFs, and Office documents are handled on the machine.

evidence.quote: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter.
Run Firecrawl on your own machine as one binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into your AI agent as an MCP server and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost.

Use the hosted service at firecrawl.dev for everything Local does at scale with nothing to run, plus search and the 550+ data providers in Firecrawl Alexandria for far more knowledge than scraping alone.
Firecrawl Local scrapes, crawls and maps from your own machine without a database, queue or container, and it reaches Firecrawl Cloud when your AI agents need search or Alexandria.
It installs from crates.io.
cargo install firecrawl-local
Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium already on your machine, and PDFs and Office documents are parsed locally too.
init finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex on your machine and adds Firecrawl Local to each one as an MCP server.
serve answers the Firecrawl v2 API on port 3002, so code written for Firecrawl runs against it unchanged and local routes need no API key.
Firecrawl Cloud runs everything Firecrawl Local does at scale, with no browser or machine of your own to look after.
It also gives your AI agents access to far more knowledge than scraping alone, with search, Alexandria, Interact and Agent all through a single API.

items.title: LingSante-3.1-flash targets medical reasoning with a 1-million-token context
items.summary: LingSante-3.1-flash is an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model built on Ling-3.1-flash with 560 billion total parameters, 25 billion activated per token, and a 1-million-token context window. It is trained to unify medical reasoning and workflow execution through native medical-mixed pretraining, mid-training, supervised fine-tuning, task-specific reinforcement learning, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation, and is intended for research and evaluation rather than as a medical device.

evidence.quote: LingSante-3.1-flash is an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model that combines complex medical reasoning, professional healthcare communication, evidence-based deep research, and long-horizon medical tasks.
Built on Ling-3.1-flash , it has 560 billion total parameters , activates 25 billion parameters per token , and supports a 1-million-token context window .

To address these demands, LingSante-3.1-flash is trained to unify medical reasoning and workflow execution through native medical-mixed pretraining, mid-training, supervised fine-tuning, task-specific reinforcement learning, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation.
The model can verify evidence across scenarios, deliver professional judgments, and independently complete multi-stage workflows.
LingSante-3.1-flash is intended for research and evaluation.
It is not a medical device and must not be used as an independent basis for diagnosis, prescriptions, or treatment.
LingSante-3.1-flash demonstrates strong performance on benchmarks for medical professional behavior, ranking second overall behind only GPT-6 Astra.

items.title: KORMo-Web-11B is a bilingual GUI agent model from KAIST MLP Lab
items.summary: KORMo-Web-11B is a general-purpose bilingual model built on the KORMo foundation model family by KAIST MLP Lab, designed to preserve its original LLM and VLM capabilities while acting as a GUI agent in Korean and English browser tasks. It uses screenshots without requiring full DOM or accessibility trees, generates an inspectable reasoning step before acting, and its weights and supporting resources are openly released under Apache-2.0.

evidence.quote: KORMo-Web-11B is a general-purpose bilingual AI model built on the KORMo foundation model family , developed by KAIST MLP Lab starting from a language model trained entirely from scratch.

Unlike our Qwen-based KORMo-Web-4B and 9B models, which focus on maximizing web task performance, KORMo-Web-11B is designed to preserve its original LLM and VLM capabilities while learning to act as a GUI agent.
It can understand Korean and English text, interpret images, and complete real browser tasks by visually navigating webpages— all within a single model.
10M+ Atomic-Level Web Pretraining Samples: Large-scale Korean and English web understanding training, covering individual UI elements, their locations, layouts, functions, and states.
100K+ Web Interaction Trajectories: Bilingual browser demonstrations for learning real-world, multi-step web tasks.
Open and Commercially Usable: Model weights and supporting resources are openly released under Apache-2.0 , allowing commercial use, modification, and redistribution subject to the license terms.
We evaluated KORMo-Web-11B on 612 live-website tasks (300 English, 312 Korean) from Online-Mind2Web, using the same LLM judge across all evaluated models.
KORMo-Web-11B achieves 33.7% Korean task success , exceeding the strongest non-KORMo open-weight baseline listed above by 13.5 percentage points .
Visual-First Web Interaction: Operates primarily through screenshots without requiring full DOM or accessibility trees.
Think, Then Act: Generates an inspectable reasoning step before executing browser actions.

items.title: A paper proposes an evaluation framework for agentic robotics
items.summary: The paper argues that an Embodied System 2, formed by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, is the decision-making core of agentic robotics, where an agent observes, interprets intent, reasons, invokes skills and tools, verifies outcomes, and adapts. It proposes an evaluation framework measuring both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance, and notes that the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, evaluation framework, or research roadmap.

evidence.quote: Qi , Shizun Wang , Xinchao Wang , Ming Yang , Zhiqin Yang , Zuhao Yang , Tao Yu Abstract Agentic robotics, centered on an Embodied System 2 formed by a foundation model and embodied harness, requires a shared evaluation framework and research roadmap to achieve reliable physical autonomy.
Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks .
It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy.
Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap.
We argue that Embodied System 2 , realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness , forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics .

Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences.
Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance.

items.title: AllocFlow generates joint portfolio allocations from raw market data
items.summary: AllocFlow is an end-to-end flow-matching framework that generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories using a cross-asset flow Transformer, followed by strategy-supervised imitation and group-relative reinforcement learning. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from 27.79% to 51.38% and its Calmar ratio from 0.955 to 4.043, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of 4.90 on six further months.

evidence.quote: Xin Li , Tianyi Wei , Weisi Lin Abstract An end-to-end flow-matching framework generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories via a cross-asset flow Transformer and a two-stage imitation and group-relative reinforcement learning procedure, improving risk-adjusted returns
We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories.

To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly.

To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme : strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that r
efines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference .

On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from 27.79% to 51.38% and its Calmar ratio from 0.955 to 4.043, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of 4.90 on six further months of un

items.title: OpenSRE is an open-source CLI agent for CI/CD reliability
items.summary: OpenSRE is described as an open-source agent for CI/CD reliability that runs on your own infrastructure with your own models, reading a failed run, tracing the cause, and pushing a fix for review. It separates CI-caused failures from code-caused ones, supports repository CI overviews, fixing failing checks on a PR, and integrations such as EKS, EC2, CloudWatch, Kubernetes, Grafana, Datadog, Slack, and GitHub, and is currently in public alpha with core workflows usable but not yet fully stable.
